title: It lived up to the hype 100% #merrilywerollalong #offbroadway #theatre
transcript: so of course, I had to go see Marylee roll along. if you're wondering how I got tickets to this, I just became a New York Theatre Workshop member. they were running a deal last year where you could get all 5 shows of this season plus the last 2 of last season for about $350, which came out to $50 per show. given the fact that full price tickets to this were a hundred, $45, even if I a show or 2, $50 per show was just too good to pass up. and this show did not disappoint. recently, I've been seeing a lot more shows that I've already seen a different production of. I did see the 2019 off Broadway production of Marley, Where roll along. the more I do that, the more I'm really able to appreciate just good direction. when you see multiple productions, you're gonna see different casts that work differently with each other. you're gonna see different design elements. but sometimes what makes or breaks a good production, in my opinion, is the direction. and to show like Merely We Roll Along has so, so many fantastic options for director to play with. things like, what are you doing during the transitions? what is the age of the actors that you are choosing to tell this story? how are you going to highlight the passing of time and the relationship between these characters? Friedman in this production of Marily does such a fantastic job with this. and I would be remiss if I did not mention their performances because every single person in the show is giving a spectacular performance. obviously, the 3 leads are astounding. they are giving career performances in this. they are all going to be nominated for tony's, but I definitely don't see enough people talking about if. Crystal Joy Brown as Gussy and Katie Rose Clark as Beth because they are also fantastic in this. everybody just works so well together, and you can tell that they just love performing with each other. thing I love about the New York Theatre Workshop is just how intimate this space is. but honestly, this is a show that I think is going to transfer very well to a larger space because the production itself just feels so intimate that even if I was in the largest Broadway theater, I would still feel connected to the story. I cannot wait for this to transfer to Broadway so more people just get to see it. because this is completely sold out. I did ask about the cancellation line. they are averaging about but the first people in line are getting in line at about 4 5 in the morning. and this isn't a rush line where you get tickets at 10 am when the box office opens. this is a line where you get tickets as they are getting canceled. so it's not a guarantee, and oftentimes you are having to wait until literally curtain time. if you are willing to do the cancellation line, definitely do it. keep entering the lottery. I know of a few people that have actually been able to win. but we already know the show is going to Broadway, so if you don't get tickets this time, can see it then. and trust me, it is worth seeing. it's honestly just exciting to see a production of Marily that does the story justice and proves that it does work as a show.
